subject.title: fix(agents): keep queued replies alive across lane waits and make stuck recovery truthful

question: Should global-lane admission be treated as indefinitely healthy waiting, or should the product define a bounded admission timeout and explicit user feedback when the shared lane remains saturated?
rationale: The patch deliberately suppresses stale recovery while global capacity is unavailable; choosing the acceptable maximum wait and failure behavior is an operational product policy that tests alone cannot settle.

options.title: Require bounded live proof first
options.body: Keep the current design pending a redacted saturated-gateway run that proves admission and an intentional bounded failure path.

options.title: Accept indefinite lane waiting
options.body: Approve the recovery fence as-is and accept that user-visible feedback may occur only after a different execution failure path.

recommendation.title: Require bounded live proof first
recommendation.body: Keep the current design pending a redacted saturated-gateway run that proves admission and an intentional bounded failure path.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied PR history places this contributor closest to the proposed lane and recovery behavior, while the protected maintainer label requires an explicit maintainer decision.
